description: Tithi start and end instants - the sharpest test of Moon-Sun elongation, and the quantity most sensitive to delta-T at historical dates.

source.notes: UNPOPULATED. Do not fill from this engine's own output - that would be a regression baseline, and the runner rejects it. Needs a published almanac, observatory table, or an authority the maintainer designates.

tolerance.rationale: Tithi boundaries are printed to the minute in almanacs, and the elongation rate near a boundary means a small longitude difference becomes a larger time difference. 180 s reflects that amplification; see docs/timescale-contract.md section 3 for why BCE entries would need far wider tolerance.

todo: Needs tithi end times for a month from an authoritative Nepali patro. Modern dates first. BCE entries should NOT be added without the uncertainty envelope from docs/timescale-contract.md section 3 attached - at 3000 BCE a tithi end time carries roughly +/- 2 h from delta-T alone, so a tight golden value there would be false precision.
